title: Reconstruct Original Digits from English
descriptionHtml:
Given a string s containing an out-of-order English representation of digits 0-9, return the digits in ascending order.

 

Example 1:

Input: s = "owoztneoer"
Output: "012"

Example 2:

Input: s = "fviefuro"
Output: "45"

 

Constraints:

  • 1 <= s.length <= 105
  • s[i] is one of the characters ["e","g","f","i","h","o","n","s","r","u","t","w","v","x","z"].
  • s is guaranteed to be valid.
explanationMarkdown:
> **Thinking**
>
> English digit words overlap, so matching words in order is unsafe. A few letters belong to only one digit.
>
> $\texttt{z}$ is unique to zero, $\texttt{w}$ to two, $\texttt{u}$ to four, $\texttt{x}$ to six, $\texttt{g}$ to eight. After subtracting those, $\texttt{h}$, $\texttt{f}$, $\texttt{s}$ give three, five, seven, and finally $\texttt{o}$ and $i$ give one and nine.
>
> Counting along that unique-letter order solves a triangular system; concatenate digits from $0$ to $9$.

solutions.label: Python 3
solutions.code:
class Solution:
    def originalDigits(self, s: str) -> str:
        counter = Counter(s)
        cnt = [0] * 10

        cnt[0] = counter['z']
        cnt[2] = counter['w']
        cnt[4] = counter['u']
        cnt[6] = counter['x']
        cnt[8] = counter['g']

        cnt[3] = counter['h'] - cnt[8]
        cnt[5] = counter['f'] - cnt[4]
        cnt[7] = counter['s'] - cnt[6]

        cnt[1] = counter['o'] - cnt[0] - cnt[2] - cnt[4]
        cnt[9] = counter['i'] - cnt[5] - cnt[6] - cnt[8]

        return ''.join(cnt[i] * str(i) for i in range(10))
